passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Enacted text of the bill Wilmeth co-sponsored and voted for; the added section makes every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified ESA student.
Official bill-status page listing Wilmeth as a co-sponsor of HB2853, signed into law as Chapter 388.
House Third Reading roll call recording Wilmeth voting Y; the 31-26 split is not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Wilmeth co-sponsored and voted Y on HB2853 (2022), a single-subject Arizona empowerment scholarship account bill whose new section 15-2401.01 makes "qualified student" include any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in preschool for children with disabilities, kindergarten, or "Any of grades one through twelve", with the state transferring the per-pupil monies that would otherwise go to the student's district into the account for tuition at a nongovernmental school or for "Services provided by a public school". That is "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family", not "Expanding voucher eligibility to most families", because the enacted end state is every public-school-eligible student rather than most.
